steps.text: Pierce the chicken breasts evenly with a fork so they soak up the marinade.
Pour salad dressing into a large resealable plastic bag; add chicken breasts, seal bag, and shake to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour to overnight.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Remove chicken from marinade and place in a lightly greased 9x13-inch baking dish; pour some of the marinade over the chicken and discard remaining marinade.

Bake uncovered in the preheated oven, turning chicken occasionally and basting it with the marinade, until cooked through and juices run clear, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Italian Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Everyone loves Italian chicken recipes, and this one’s a winner. Italian-style dressing plus boneless breasts make a tender, tasty, 2-ingredient dish.

review.reviewBody: I've been using this recipe for years and it's still one of our favorites. The only thing we do differently is cook the chicken in the italian dressing at a low heat (275 degrees) for 2 or 3 hours or until the chicken browns. It comes out tender and delicious and we use the left over cooked dressing to "dip" the chicken, our seven year old granddaughter's favorite thing to do!

This is the easiest and most delicious chicken recipe!!! I make it for my roommates at least once a week, it is one of their favorites!! Before marinating the chicken I make sure to poke holes in it with a fork to let the marinate soak in, as another reviewer suggested. I use a zesty Italian dressing and usually throw it together before leaving for work, 9 hours later it has a great flavor and makes a quick meal. To give it an extra kick, before cooking I usually take a few pieces and dip each side in a bowl of parmasean cheese. I'm not a fan of the extra cheesy taste but everyone else loves it that way!! Cook this with the Oven Roasted Potatoes recipe from this site and you have an easy and delicious meal that people will love!!

I marinated 3 large chicken breasts in Wishbone Italian dressing for 6 hours then placed them in a baking dish sprayed with olive oil. I cooked them covered with aluminum foil for an hour, then removed the foil and cooked them on 350 using convection for another 30 minutes. Convection browned them to a more pleasing hue without drying them out too much. These could also be easily cooked in the air fryer following similar instructions. They turned out delicious. I served them with broccoli and rice casserole.

Instead of using store-bought salad dressing, the Italian in me makes my own - just EVOO, red wine vinegar, some Italian herbs and that's it. Works for me and has through my 53 years of marriage, 3 children and 3 grands. Not to mention a batch of sisters (4) and one brother who visit often. This is a simple go-to recipe that can be doubled and even tripled, depending on the number of folks you'll be serving. Sides of potatoes (or rice, or buttery noodles) and veggies, a good salad, round out a very nice, easy meal, guest worthy for sure.

This turned out really really good! I tweaked it bun adding black pepper to the chicken after marinating it. I used Ken’s Steakhouse Light version of Italian dressing to marinate and bake the chicken in. I also removed the chicken from the oven 15 minutes prior to finish and spooned Parmesan cheese over the top of each piece of chicken breast, then sprinkled on some chopped crispy bacon and let it finish cooking for 15 minutes to melt and brown the Parmesan cheese. I also tenderized my chicken before baking it by pounding it with a small meat mallet and covered the dish with foil for the first 45 minutes of baking to prevent the chicken from drying out during baking. Everyone at dinner loved it and I do plan to make it again. Thanks for sharing!!

I make with Italian dressing and seasoning. I don't marinade. Just a bit of butter, with dressing and seasoning and just bake. Flip once...comes out a little prettier...browned. Too easy. Made it, for years.

This recipe is super simple and tasty but the chicken turned out far too dry when I discarded the marinade so when I remade it I cooked it with the remaining marinade hoping it would retain the moisture and flavor, I also added some crushed garlic and black pepper and it turned out fantastic.

Excellent basic recipe that can be developed further by keeping the marinade & adding veggies to it. First of all I do salt the chicken well letting it set a few hours or overnight, then a few hours before baking add the dressing ( Wishbone- Italian). One hour before baking cover the chicken with 28 " can of diced tomatoes, 3 cloves garlic slivered, 1 sliced carrot, 1 celery stalk sliced & 1 onion halved & sliced. Also Cacciatore style, olives & raisins could be added.
While chicken is baking, blend a heaping handful of fresh garden parsley to put onto the chicken & sauce before turning over the breasts after baking 1/2 hr , saving half of the parsley to put onto the rotini noodles. Bake about another 20 minutes or so. I then shred zucchini to cook with the noodles 2 minutes before noodles are done. 
Also I use 4-5 large breast. When baked& cooled a bit, slice them vertically into 4-6 slices per breast 
& serve with sauce over breasts & noodles. A handful of chopped or blended basil is nice.
I did this in the air fryer to cut the cooking time to 15 minutes! A go-to when I need something easy!

I totally forgot all about this recipe! Today I used two chicken breast, marinated it for an hour, topped it with fresh minced garlic, sweet basil, rosemary, onions, and red, green and orange bell peppers. I am cooking it in NewWave oven to prevent heating up the entire house. I wrapped the chicken in foil but will open the top after it cooks for 30 minutes and allow it to cook another 30 minutes. I can't wait for the aroma to fill up the house. For side dishes, I baked some potatoes and made a tossed salad. Although it is not ready to eat, I know this is going to be a delicious dish. My mouth is already watering.
I added mushrooms, onions, peppers, tomatoes and Lipton onion mix. It made a complete meal that we love!! I also serve it over linguine.
Easiest chicken I have ever made. Stayed moist, I followed the recipe.

I went according to the recipe, except I used skinless thighs. I placed the chicken and sauce over a bed of Goya seasoned black beans and rice. That added a good bit of flavor. I'll be making it again
I filet chicken breast ,pound thin,stab with fork,marinate in any italian dressing then pan fry,stuffing and green beans on side...
One hour dessicated my huge chicken breasts. Sure next time I can cook them less but it would be great if recipes just worked as written.
I didn’t care for the marinaded taste at all. It’s a good concept but maybe a different flavor would be better.
These are amazing! I sliced the breasts partially open and stuffed them with Feta and spinach. Then proceeded with the recipe. Delicious!

I haven't made it, but will soon. I'll also try it with boneless pork chops or a pork loin. Boneless skinless chicken breasts are usually dry, even when slightly undercooked. Perhaps this method will improve the outcome. For my husband I'll use thighs and legs since he prefers those.

I've made this recipes many times. Although I do like it, and its extremely easy to make, I still think it needs some more flavor. Im usually in a hurry when I make this, so I haven't messed with the recipe to see what can give it more flavor.
It’s good. Gets to 165° way quicker that 1 or 1:30 hours like some people posted.
